context.title: Jonathan's Bold Faith
context.summary: Jonathan and his armor-bearer climb a cliff to attack a Philistine outpost, trusting God to save 'by many or by few.' Panic sweeps the enemy. But Saul's rash oath leaves his men faint, and Jonathan, who ate honey without knowing, is nearly executed until the people rescue him.
context.background: The pass at Michmash was a steep gorge between two rocky crags named Bozez and Seneh (v. 4). The priest with Saul, Ahiah, was a great-grandson of Eli (v. 3). The starving troops ate meat with the blood still in it (v. 32), breaking a basic food law.

customs.note: A Hebrew way of saying his strength was renewed; tired eyes brightened as he ate.

watchFor: 'There is no restraint to the Lord to save by many or by few' (v. 6).
Jonathan says his father's oath has 'troubled the land' (v. 29).
The people ransom Jonathan from his father's vow (v. 45).

people.name: Saul
people.summary: The son of Kish (probably his only son, and a child of prayer, “asked for”), of the tribe of Benjamin, the first king of the Jewish nation. The singular providential circumstances connected with his election as king are recorded in 1 Sam. 8-10.

people.name: Jonathan
people.summary: The eldest son of king Saul, and the bosom friend of David. He is first mentioned when he was about thirty years of age, some time after his father’s accession to the throne (1 Sam. 13:2).

people.name: Eli
people.summary: Ascent, the high priest when the ark was at Shiloh (1 Sam. 1:3, 9). He was the first of the line of Ithamar, Aaron’s fourth son (1 Chr. 24:3; comp. 2 Sam. 8:17), who held that office.

people.name: Ahimelech
people.summary: Son of Ahitub (1 Sam. 14:3, 18), Ichabod’s brother; the same probably as Ahimelech, who was high priest at Nob in the reign of Saul (1 Sam. 22:11).

people.name: Phinehas
people.summary: One of the sons of Eli, the high priest (1 Sam. 1:3; 2:12). He and his brother Hophni were guilty of great crimes, for which destruction came on the house of Eli (31).

people.name: Ahitub
people.summary: The son of Phinehas.

people.name: Benjamin
people.summary: The younger son of Jacob by Rachel (Gen. 35:18). His birth took place at Ephrath, on the road between Bethel and Bethlehem, at a short distance from the latter place.

people.name: Israel
people.summary: One who follows on another’s heels; supplanter, (Gen. 25:26; 27:36; Hos. 12:2-4), the second born of the twin sons of Isaac by Rebekah. He was born probably at Lahai-roi, when his father was fifty-nine and Abraham one hundred and fifty-nine years old.

people.name: Ephraim
people.summary: Double fruitfulness (“for God had made him fruitful in the land of his affliction”). The second son of Joseph, born in Egypt (Gen. 41:52; 46:20).

people.name: Esau
people.summary: Hairy, Rebekah’s first-born twin son (Gen. 25:25). The name of Edom, “red”, was also given to him from his conduct in connection with the red lentil “pottage” for which he sold his birthright (30, 31).

people.name: Moab
people.summary: Used to denote the people of Moab (Num. 22:3-14; Judg. 3:30; 2 Sam. 8:2; Jer. 48:11, 13).

people.name: Michal
people.summary: Rivulet, or who as God?, the younger of Saul’s two daughters by his wife Ahinoam (1 Sam. 14:49, 50). “Attracted by the graces of his person and the gallantry of his conduct, she fell in love with David and became his wife” (18:20-28).

people.name: Abinadab
people.summary: One of Saul’s sons, who peristed with his father in the battle of Gilboa (1 Sam. 31:2; 1 Chr. 10:2).

people.name: Merab
people.summary: Increase, the eldest of Saul’s two daughters (1 Sam. 14:49). She was betrothed to David after his victory over Goliath, but does not seem to have entered heartily into this arrangement (18:2, 17, 19).

people.name: Abner
people.summary: Father of light; i.e., “enlightening”, the son of Ner and uncle of Saul. He was commander-in-chief of Saul’s army (1 Sam. 14:50; 17:55; 20:25).

people.name: Ner
people.summary: Light, the father of Kish (1 Chr. 8:33). 1 Sam. 14:51 should be read, “Kish, the father of Saul, and Ner, the father of Abner, were the sons of Abiel.”

people.name: Ahimaaz
people.summary: The father Ahinoam, the wife of Saul (1 Sam. 14:50).

people.name: Ahinoam
people.summary: The daughter of Ahimaaz, and wife of Saul (1 Sam. 14:50).

people.name: Kish
people.summary: A Benjamite, the son of Abiel, and father of king Saul (1 Sam. 9:1, 3; 10:11, 21; 14:51; 2 Sam. 21:14). All that is recorded of him is that he sent his son Saul in search of his asses that had strayed, and that he was buried in Zelah.

people.name: Abiel
people.summary: The son of Zeror and father of Ner, who was the grandfather of Saul (1 Sam. 14:51; 1 Chr. 8:33; 9:39).

places.name: Gibeah
places.summary: A hill or hill-town, “of Benjamin” (1 Sam. 13:15), better known as “Gibeah of Saul” (11:4; Isa. 10:29). It was here that the terrible outrage was committed on the Levite’s concubine which led to the almost utter extirpation of the tribe of Benjamin (Judg. 19; 20), only six hundred men surviving after a succession of disastrous battles.

places.name: Migron
places.summary: Precipice or landslip, a place between Aiath and Michmash (Isa. 10:28).

places.name: Shiloh
places.summary: Generally understood as denoting the Messiah, “the peaceful one,” as the word signifies (Gen. 49:10). The Vulgate Version translates the word, “he who is to be sent,” in allusion to the Messiah; the Revised Version, margin, “till he come to Shiloh;” and the LXX., “until that which is his shall come to Shiloh.”

places.name: Seneh
places.summary: The acacia; rock-thorn, the southern cliff in the Wady es-Suweinit, a valley south of Michmash, which Jonathan climbed with his armour-bearer (1 Sam. 14:4, 5).

places.name: Michmash
places.summary: Something hidden, a town of Benjamin (Ezra 2:27), east of Bethel and south of Migron, on the road to Jerusalem (Isa. 10:28). It lay on the line of march of an invading army from the north, on the north side of the steep and precipitous Wady es-Suweinit (“valley of the little thorn-tree” or “the acacia”), and now bears the name of Mukhmas.

places.name: Beth-aven
places.summary: House of nothingness; i.e., “of idols”, a place in the mountains of Benjamin, east of Bethel (Josh. 7:2; 18:12; 1 Sam. 13:5).

places.name: Aijalon
places.summary: A city in the tribe of Zebulun (Judg. 12:12), the modern Jalun, three miles north of Cabul.

places.name: Edom
places.summary: Idumea (Isa. 34:5, 6; Ezek. 35:15). “The field of Edom” (Gen. 32:3), “the land of Edom” (Gen. 36:16), was mountainous (Obad. 1:8, 9, 19, 21).

places.name: Moab
places.summary: The land of Moab (Jer. 48:24), called also the “country of Moab” (Ruth 1:2, 6; 2:6), on the east of Jordan and the Dead Sea, and south of the Arnon (Num. 21:13, 26).

places.name: Zobah
places.summary: Aram-Zobah, (Ps. 60, title), a Syrian province or kingdom to the south of Coele-Syria, and extending from the eastern slopes of Lebanon north and east toward the Euphrates.

events.title: Reign of Saul
events.summary: Passage: 1 Samuel 10:1–31:2. People: Saul. Lasted about 40 years.
